rows.name: fib
rows.note: Bounded recursive expansion halves raw calls; remaining int53 poison/overflow and real deeper calls are preserved (S4.1.2).

rows.name: fibfp
rows.note: Bounded expansion halves raw calls and it2d conversions; floating evaluation order is unchanged.

rows.name: tak
rows.note: Already raw scalar recursion with no root reloads; the existing tail-call path is retained. Residual JS gap needs native-code attribution.

rows.name: cpstak
rows.note: Both current ports run direct Tak twice; neither executes CPS closures. Raw recursion and the existing tail-call path remain. The old Lambda comment is not a diagnosis.

rows.name: sumfp
rows.note: Both sources descend with a floating counter. No hot generic helpers or root reloads were measured; an integer-counter explanation would be incorrect. Residual gap is unresolved.

rows.name: nqueens
rows.note: Lambda mutates a plain placed parameter under snapshot semantics; JS uses shared Int32Array storage. The profile retains allocation and mutation work. Numeric-call tuning does not prove those snapshots redundant (S9.1.2).

rows.name: fft
rows.note: Lambda takes a plain data parameter and uses open numeric operations; JS uses Float64Array and integer bit shifts. Generic index/arithmetic helpers remain. The zero-input result is not proof of caller write-back equivalence.

rows.name: ack
rows.note: Already native scalar recursion, with no hot helpers or roots. Real recursive edges and integer semantics remain; scalar expansion is not unrestricted.

rows.name: list
rows.note: Linked-list recursion retains 38,216 generic member reads and nullable records. Member-assignment candidates do not prove recursive constructor-result shapes. JS uses reference-linked class instances.

rows.name: mandelbrot
rows.note: The Lambda spelling retains 250,000 generic adds in packed-byte construction. The scalar loop policy does not infer a complete range for a repeatedly shifted byte accumulator. JS uses machine-word bitwise arithmetic.

rows.name: richards
rows.note: Lambda uses a COW-safe handle store indexed through one var root, whereas the JS scheduler uses reference-linked tasks/packets. 8,656,300 generic index calls remain; source representation is not matched.

rows.name: cd
rows.note: Guarded record reads remove the remaining generic member helpers, but 16.7 million index calls and 15.1 million equality calls remain. Their CPU shares are not established by counts; no claim of a complete record-workload speedup.

rows.name: binarytrees
rows.note: Both ports allocate/check trees, but the boxed recursive tree boundary, allocation and descriptor reads remain. Scalar-only inlining excludes container results. Value semantics alone does not prove this read-only workload needs copies.

rows.name: pidigits
rows.note: The Lambda port uses arbitrary-precision decimal n values and quotient via remainder/subtraction; JS uses BigInt and division with sign adjustment. Do not narrow this to int53 merely to match JS.

rows.name: brainfuck
rows.note: Phase 2 is already in this fresh control. JS also uses a byte tape, mask, else-if dispatch and joined output; Lambda retains integer tape, remainder, independent ifs and string output. No incremental predicate win is expected here.

rows.name: base64
rows.note: Raw string length/entry admission removes one boxed boundary per iteration, while 1,333,500 string concatenations and 666,600 index calls remain. JS uses Uint8Array and fragments/join; ports are not representation matched.

rows.name: levenshtein
rows.note: Native producer/length/array/scalar paths eliminate most generic indexing/arithmetic and roots. min3 still takes possibly absent arguments through its boxed entry; no partial tuple is asserted fully admitted (D8.3.3). JS also uses typed arrays and a hoisted character read.

rows.name: json_gen
rows.note: Forwarded string facts enable existing join fusion, but bounded admission leaves some boxed calls/joins. Both already use the owned outer builder. Floor versus Math.trunc for negative coordinates also prevents a full-content JS parity claim from the length oracle alone.

rows.name: collatz
rows.note: 999,999 generic comparisons remain. Lambda shr(n,1) and JS division by two have different intermediate machine-word semantics; the full dynamic trajectory has no established finite range proof.

rows.name: triangl
rows.note: Both run backtracking, with Lambda bool/int arrays versus JS Uint8Array/Int32Array and different break spelling. Already-native loops have no hot generic helper traffic; remaining indexed/induction guards need their own proofs.

rows.name: array1
rows.note: Already-native array loops; JS uses Int32Array. Helper elimination cannot explain this residual gap. No numeric-conversion consumer exists to justify the additional scalar-copy policy.

rows.name: deriv
rows.note: Heterogeneous expression-tree tags/fields retain 865,000 generic member reads, allocation and boxed recursion. A single guarded candidate is not a general recursive sum-type specialization.

rows.name: gcbench
rows.note: Boxed container-result recursion and allocation remain, including 3,222,190 map allocations. Descriptor reads improve independently; this is not evidence that all copies or allocation work is redundant.

rows.name: paraffins
rows.note: Scalar multiset helpers inline, while nullable indexed operands still need checked admission. JS uses Int32Array and else-if partitioning; Lambda uses independent conditions and int53 arithmetic.

rows.name: puzzle
rows.note: 174,909 numeric-array copies preserve mutated plain-parameter snapshots. JS uses shared arrays and undo. Removing the copies would change the unchanged Lambda source contract (S9.1.2-S9.1.3).

rows.name: iteration_pi_sum
rows.note: Imported hot-function assembly proves the finite affine induction/conversion reduction. Floating addition/division and evaluation order are unchanged. Both Lambda columns use the same source.

rows.name: fast_diff
rows.note: Native length/array/scalar flow removes the generic LCS inner-loop operations. The untyped Lambda port still uses LCS and the JS port uses Myers/bisection; the timed typed port includes preprocessing. A remaining cross-language ratio is not an isolated compiler comparison.

rows.name: prettier_ast
rows.note: Record constructors keep boxed string forwarding when it would only add conversions. Recursive mixed AST nodes retain 26.6 million generic member reads and boxed calls. Final diagnostics match control counts; the rejected admission policy is excluded.

rows.name: text_search
rows.note: Producer/nullable-branch/call facts remove most Boyer-Moore generic arithmetic and root reloads. Remaining 3,283,291 generic reads preserve paths without complete bounds/shape proofs.

rows.name: three_way_merge
rows.note: 33 million checked lengths, push/COW and generic index paths remain on collection-producing helpers. String-valued scalar forwarding does not certify these string-array layouts or eliminate observable copies.

rows.name: navier_stokes
rows.note: The hot loops were already native; Lambda content swaps differ from JS reference swaps and the JS port combines a solver pass. The retained 1.47 million floor/conversion calls are not eliminated by an integer-to-double proof.

rows.name: splay
rows.note: All 2,622,536 generic member calls become live-descriptor guarded reads. The 951,168 value-tree map copies remain, especially splay_node and rotations with retained local owners. Source rebuilds differ from JS mutable links (S9.1.2-S9.1.3).

rows.name: crypto_sha1
rows.note: Bounded rol and scalar expansion reduce calls/roots; nullable array inputs and fallible machine-word operations retain ordinary helpers. Explicit wrap/shift and error semantics are preserved (S4.1.5).
